added_failures_note: read from the reviewed run's own logs/reviewer arms: review.added_failures_from_gate_logs (logs/base.log, logs/gate.log) returns 3 with the head node ids carrying the gate log's ../../home/... invocation prefix; stripping that one prefix leaves both arms' id sets identical, so the count by node id is 0 and the three ids are the pre-existing tests/test_fleet_counter_coverage.py failures present at both revisions. The production read path reports this run unmeasured because the manifest's baseline_suite/after_suite lines carry prose rather than a log path — see finding 1.

findings.text: the baseline_suite and after_suite fields carry prose summaries where the fleet reader expects a log path (the two shapes review._gate_log_path accepts), so review.annotate_review_of_run resolves the prose line as a path, cannot open it, and stores added_failure_count None with "unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log"; the run's zero-added-by-id claim is therefore unreadable by the very instrument the promotion path reads, and the two logs it does name live under test_logs, a field that reader does not consult.

the head arm's FAILED lines carry the invocation prefix ../../home/ITER/mcintos/Code/.reckon-worktrees/reckon-c8f839407e49/s21-coord/a-promotion-never-reads-unpromoted/ while the base arm's are relative, so review.added_failures_from_gate_logs(base, head) returns 3 added failures naming three tests that are green at both revisions; stripping that one prefix leaves the two id sets identical (measured both readings), so a log produced with a different cwd spelling turns a pre-existing failure into a phantom regression for every reader of this run.

the refused-dispatch and vanished-reflex-review routes are asserted only as != "promoted" — line 244 and line 253 compare against the negated word — so a regression renaming withdrawn to any other non-promoted value satisfies the test while §3's requirement that a vanished reflex review be reported as withdrawn goes unguarded; the same tests hand the fold an explicit ledger reader, so the production resolution branch in recovery._departure_recorded_run_ids (reader resolved from the departing run's project) is never exercised.

findings: FINDING reckon/crew/recovery.py:5285 the three departure routes still never render promoted, verified true: a refused dispatch and a vanished reflex review depart withdrawn and a deliberate discard departs discarded, because _departure_word returns the promoted word only when the run id is in the recorded set read from the departing run's own project ledger; my base arm passes all four departure tests, so this property predates the reviewed change and the reviewed change leaves it intact.
